title: Critical N-able N-central Flaw Enables Unauthenticated Pre-Auth Remote Code Execution
content_md: N-able has issued an urgent security update for a critical vulnerability in its N-central remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform that could let an unauthenticated attacker execute code on a vulnerable server before logging in. Tracked as CVE-2026-86218, the issue is fixed in N-central 2026.3 Hotfix 4, build 2026.3.1.14. N-central is used by managed service providers and IT teams to administer endpoints and customer environments from a central console. A pre-authentication remote code execution flaw is especially serious in that role: exploitation would not require valid N-central credentials, potentially giving an attacker a foothold on the management server that can span the administered infrastructure. Critical N-able N-central Flaw N-able has rated CVE-2026-86218 as critical, but has not published technical root-cause details, affected components, a CVSS numeric score, proof-of-concept code, or indicators of compromise. The bug was responsibly disclosed through the vendor’s security disclosure program. N-able said it has no confirmed evidence of exploitation in production environments as of the advisory’s publication; that statement should not be treated as evidence that exposed self-hosted servers are safe to defer patching. The remediation is included in N-central 2026.3 Hotfix 4, released as build 2026.3.1.14 and superseding Hotfix 3, build 2026.3.1.13. Direct upgrades to the new build are supported from versions 2025.4, 2026.1, 2026.2, 2026.3, and 2026.3.1 Hot
